title: Linked List Cycle
description:
A singly linked list has n nodes holding the given values, in order. The last node's next pointer either points to nothing or back to an earlier node (a cycle). Decide whether the list contains a cycle.

Input format
Line 1: n and pos separated by a space. pos is the 0-based index of the node that the last node points back to, or -1 if the last node points to nothing.
Line 2: n integers, the node values (values may repeat; they say nothing about the structure).

Output format
YES if the list has a cycle, otherwise NO.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. -1 <= pos < n. Values fit in a 32-bit signed integer.
hints: If you walk the list and ever reach a node you have already visited, what does that tell you?
Remember visited nodes (by position, not by value) in a set. Reaching the end of the list means there is no cycle.
Floyd's algorithm needs no extra memory: move one pointer one step and another two steps at a time. If they ever meet, there is a cycle. Do not compare node values - duplicates are allowed.

examples.explanation: The last node points back to index 1, forming a cycle.
The last node points to nothing.
